A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TFL/TMP research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial layout changes and reordered appendix sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments on five datasets, annotation-error measurements, component ablations and hyperparameter sensitivity results.

after.justification: v2 retains original classification and ablation results and adds a CLIP pseudo-label baseline and measured training-time comparisons.

M1.justification: The frozen CLIP backbone, convolutional prompt network, retrieval components, probability mixture, training loss and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Equation (9) explicitly inserts the image encoder gI(x), consistent with the encoder already shown in v1's Figure 2; this does not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR-100, Tiny ImageNet, Caltech-101, Food-101 and Stanford Cars using VLM-generated and ground-truth-derived TFLs. The added timing experiment uses two existing datasets without introducing a new task, population or test environment.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds CLIP LPP, a linear probe trained on CLIP pseudo-labels, and removes the ground-truth-supervised probe from that comparison; the latter remains in Table 3 as CLIP LPS. OCRA becoming ORCA and the existing TFL probe becoming CLIP LPT are naming changes, not new comparators.

E3.justification: The new CLIP LPP comparison trains on CLIP pseudo-labels for all training examples. Section 4.6 introduces average seconds per epoch on CIFAR-100 and Caltech-101 using one RTX 4090. Existing classification settings, including ViT-L/14, training budgets, batch size and optimizers, remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.6 adds a computational-efficiency analysis comparing TMP with weakly supervised methods. Table 4 revises the evidence from the existing component-removal ablations, while retaining their datasets and variants. The lambda sensitivity analysis in Figure 3 remains unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. The added average training times do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Main TMP accuracies remain unchanged. v2 adds CLIP LPP results averaging 81.14% and training-time results. Table 4 changes Stanford Cars scores without MPR/TPR/VPR from 69.44/70.09/70.15 to 71.25/72.25/72.53, retaining full TMP at 72.60. Table 1 corrects the labeling-speed average from 174.75, inconsistently stated as 174.25 in v1's prose, to 69.9.

T1.justification: The theorem proof in v2 Appendix A.2, formerly A.3, restores a missing outer summation over class i in the risk expansion. This corrects an intermediate mathematical expression. The underlying assumptions, lemma and risk identity otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain high-quality, efficient TFL annotation, a risk-consistent estimator and convolutional multi-modal prompt retrieval. The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain these claims and their scope; additional comparisons and mechanism discussion do not redefine them.

C2.justification: v2 shifts the motivating explanation from out-of-vocabulary labeling to incorrect CLIP predictions and adds substantive arguments about implicit regularization, bias mitigation, true-label semantic anchors and CNN locality. It replaces v1's limitation about unresolved VLM mislabeling with lack of test-time adaptation. The discussion of approaching fully supervised performance is also narrowed to Food-101.

D1.justification: Table 1 newly discloses true-label counts, Appendix A.3 states the CNN's 150,531 parameters, and the ablation and sensitivity captions explicitly identify human-derived TFLs. Section 4.6 documents timing measurements and hardware. These additions do not establish changes to the retained architecture, hyperparameters or code access.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting stochastic regularization, annotation errors, visual prompting and recent weakly supervised learning, including Ali et al., Northcutt et al., Bahng et al. and Wang et al. It extends comparisons with self-training and direct prompt optimization while preserving the main related-work organization and novelty positioning.

P1.justification: Targeted edits revise introductory and experimental prose, replace manual with human-based terminology, update author and affiliation information, and move appendix proofs before the architecture description. Acknowledgements and an impact statement are added. Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 extensively reformats the main text into two columns, redesigns Figure 1 around CLIP and human annotation, adds the training-time chart, expands Table 1 and rearranges or resizes retained displays. The appendix network diagram moves from Figure 4 to Figure 5, retaining its content.

improvement.justification: The direct pseudo-label baseline addresses a useful missing comparison, while measured training costs and corrections to the speed average and proof improve the paper's evidence and precision. These gains are limited by reporting weaknesses: revised Table 4 implies component gains of 0.39 and 0.15 percentage points despite claiming more than 0.5, and the earlier label-noise limitation disappears. The added relevant control and corrections nevertheless support a limited net improvement.
